sentences.text: Asilisaurus kongwe is the type species of an extinct genus of silesaurid archosaurs, a family to which the animal belongs.
This lightly built creature possessed a long neck, a short beaked snout, and slender limbs, standing between half a meter and one meter tall while measuring one to three meters in length.
Its skull featured a unique lack of teeth at the front of the premaxilla, which is the bone at the very tip of the upper jaw, and a downturned, toothless tip on its lower jaw.

The skeleton included two sacral vertebrae with individual sacral ribs, a long narrow scapula expanded into a triangular tip without perforations, and a closed acetabulum in the hip that distinguishes it from the open acetabulum found in dinosaurs.
Asilisaurus was the first non-dinosaur dinosauromorph recovered from Africa and the first non-dinosaur dinosauriform discovered on the continent.
One femur specimen was estimated to be 29.6-39.6 cm long, more than twice the length of other known Asilisaurus femurs.
It is the oldest known archosaur on the avian lineage discovered to date.
The first remains of Asilisaurus were found in 2007 at a bonebed near Litumba Ndyosi in Tanzania.

The genus was described in 2010 by a team of researchers from the United States, Germany, and South Africa, with the generic name derived from the Swahili word for 'ancestor' and the Greek word for 'lizard'.
The specific name kongwe means 'ancient' in Swahili.
Based on limb length, Asilisaurus probably walked on all four legs, and studies confirm it apparently moved by walking on four legs.
Evidence of a beak and peg-like teeth suggests Asilisaurus was likely an omnivore or herbivore, and the conical shape of its teeth suggests that fish may have been part of its diet.

Studies of femurs revealed multiple polymorphic trajectories in muscle scar development rather than a universal sequence, and histological analysis showed no lines of arrested growth, even in large specimens.
Researchers hypothesize that the absence of these growth lines does not mean specimens died within a year, as their growth rate was too slow for that.
Asilisaurus is classified within the family Silesauridae and the class Ornithischia.
At least 14 specimens of Asilisaurus were found in southern Tanzania dating to the Anisian stage of the Middle Triassic.
Asilisaurus represents the first example of the avian lineage radiation during the Anisian period.
Some authors suggest the Manda Beds formation may date to the Ladinian or early Carnian stages instead of the Anisian.
Researchers suggest that Asilisaurus implies dinosaurs may be older than previously thought.
